findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", which is effectively administrative control over compute, storage and serverless resources in the account. Combined with ec2/lambda access this also enables privilege escalation via iam:PassRole-adjacent paths and data exfiltration from any S3 bucket.

A permanent IAM access key is provisioned for a service user instead of using a role with temporary credentials; the key never expires unless manually rotated and its secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext when no PGP key is supplied.

A long-lived IAM user with a highly privileged inline policy is created rather than an assumable role with a permissions boundary, so there is no guardrail against privilege escalation and no automatic credential expiry.

The secret key material is exposed through the Terraform output 'svc_deploy_key_material' without sensitive = true, so it is printed to the console and CI logs and persisted in state accessible to anyone with state read access.
